answer: A single juniper checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called a pulse, before it can post or attest. Forging 348 aliases therefore burns 122 bonds held for 12 days each, plus the sonnet attestations those aliases can never earn. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
